references.text: Jacob asks Joseph to swear that he will not bury him in Egypt, but with his ancestors. This is the first time Jacob expresses his wish to be buried in Canaan.

Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah and the field from Ephron the Hittite as a burial place. It is this cave that Jacob refers to when he asks to be buried 'in the cave that is on the field of Ephron the Hittite'.
Abraham is buried by Isaac and Ishmael in the cave of Machpelah, the same cave that Jacob now asks to be laid in, to rest with his ancestors.
Isaac dies and 'was gathered to his people' – the same expression that Jacob uses about himself (נֶאֱסָף אֶל־עַמִּי). Isaac was buried by Esau and Jacob.
The continuation where Jacob specifies that the cave is in the field of Machpelah near Mamre in Canaan, and mentions that Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, and Leah are buried there.
Jacob's sons fulfill his last wish and bury him in the cave of Machpelah, as he had asked them to do.
Both express a deep theological desire to be gathered with a righteous person in death to preserve fellowship beyond life.
This is a direct narrative link where Jacob in 49:29 refers to the specific transaction and the ground secured in chapter 23.
Both verses connect the patriarchs' deaths to the promise of the land and express faith that they will be gathered with their fathers in Canaan.
The verses illuminate each other as respectively the purchase of the land and the final use of the same cave for the patriarch's burial.
Both verses emphasize God's eternal promise of the land as the foundation for the patriarchs' identity and burial wish.
Both verses use the theological term 'gathered to the fathers' as a sign of dying in peace and the continuity of faith.
